ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All proposed directors, shareholders and beneficial owners must, before incorporation, be screened against the FIC Targeted Financial Sanctions list, the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, and HM Treasury consolidated list where relevant, in accordance with s.28A of FICA and the Financial Intelligence Centre Regulations 2004. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for every politically exposed person (PEP), foreign PEP, or person connected to a PEP, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification. Screening results must be evidenced in the AML/CFT file and refreshed immediately on any sanctions-related change.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) Online Services portal (www.cipc.co.za / www.cipc.gov.za); name reservation application uses Form CoR 9.1.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Latin-script letters; where the intended name is drawn from any of South Africa's 11 official languages or a foreign language, an exact Latin-alphabet transliteration is required at reservation. The legal suffix must match the entity form: '(Pty) Ltd' for a private company, and the name must not be confusingly similar to existing registered names, according to s.11 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 and the Companies Regulations, 2011.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name rejection issued by CIPC must be cured by submitting, within 20 business days, either (i) a fresh CoR 9.1 application incorporating an additional distinctive element, or (ii) written submissions to CIPC's registration department explaining why the ground for refusal does not apply. If CIPC persists, the applicant may apply to the Companies Tribunal under s.160 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 for a review within 6 months of rejection. Reserved names may be extended before expiry using the CIPC extension module; if expiration occurs before incorporation, a new reservation application will be required.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office / non-retail mail-handling address is acceptable for CIPC registration and for a low-risk online beauty DTC retailer, provided the address is a physical address in South Africa where notices and legal process can be served. The business must, however, maintain real commercial substance, board decision-making records, and an effective place of management in South Africa; any shell arrangement or pure mail-drop may be disregarded by SARS under general anti-avoidance rules and for corporate-residence purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: estimated annual probability of an unannounced SARS physical inspection is below 5% for a low-risk, non-licensed cosmetics online retailer; CIPC will normally inspect only upon a formal complaint, insolvency event, or suspected fraud. Operational tax audits are usually desk-based unless risk flags are raised through inconsistent VAT registrations or the payment rails report activity incompatible with declared turnover.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, as amended (including Companies Amendment Acts 16 & 17 of 2024), ss. 13-14 (incorporation and registration), 19 (juridical personality), 23-24 (name and rectification), 40 (share issuance), 66 and 69 (board composition and director eligibility); Companies Regulations 2011 (GN R. 351), Regs. 9-14.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), a public agency of the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic); filings are made through the CIPC e-Services portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation on Form CoR 14.1, accompanied by the executed Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI), filed under ss. 13-14 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement for a private company; shares may be issued for consideration determined by the board under s. 40 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008, subject to the solvency and liquidity test; unissued share capital may remain in the authorized capital pool.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the company subscribes to and accepts the allotment of 100 ordinary shares to J. Doe and K. Smith as reflected in the Memorandum of Incorporation, consideration being determined by the board. RESOLVED FURTHER that the registered office at 12 Greenpoint Avenue, Cape Town, 8001 is adopted and filed with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission. RESOLVED FURTHER that J. Doe is appointed Managing Director and K. Smith Financial Director, each holding office until the next annual general meeting. RESOLVED FURTHER that the directors are authorized to open bank accounts, execute commercial agreements, and complete all statutory filings with CIPC and SARS.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Incorporator Due Diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create a CIPC e-Services user profile; file Form CoR 9.1 to reserve the proposed company name; confirm the name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing entity or trademark; submit up to two alternative names; verify each incorporator's and director's South African ID or foreign passport; scan identity documents and proof of residential address.
required_dossiers: Certified ID copies of each incorporator and director
CIPC user authorization evidence (affidavit for foreign applicants)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC refuses the name under s. 23, it issues written reasons; promptly file a revised name reservation or a Regulation 13 objection; if the objection is dismissed, appeal to the Companies Tribunal within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Memorandum of Incorporation and Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC (pre-filing preparation; documents to be lodged via e-Services)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt the CIPC standard MOI template (Form CoR 15.1A) for a private company; insert the registered office address and the identity particulars of the first directors; each incorporator signs the MOI; the registered office agent signs the consent to the office; the first directors sign consents to their appointments.
required_dossiers: Form CoR 15.1A standard Memorandum of Incorporation (executed)
Form CoR 11.1 (consent to registered office address)
Form CoR 11.3 (consent by each first director)
Completed Form CoR 14.1 signed by an incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC requires amendments for non-conforming MOI clauses, amend the document, obtain re-execution, and resubmit through the same transaction queue within the prescribed correction window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Online Submission of the Notice of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the executed MOI, consents and Form CoR 14.1; select the private company (Pty) Ltd template; confirm the registered office and director details; pay the filing fee of ZAR 175 online; record the transaction tracking number and acknowledgement email for follow-up.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC issues a notice of non-acceptance or a request for rectification, the incorporator corrects the errors and resubmits within 10 business days; if the transaction lapses, file a fresh application using the reserved name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation and Company Extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download the electronic Certificate of Incorporation bearing the company registration number (format 2026/xxxxxx/07 for private companies); retrieve and verify the company record extract; confirm that the registered office, directors and share particulars are correctly displayed.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate or extract shows typographical or legal errors, apply to CIPC for rectification of the record under s. 24 of the Companies Act; corrections are issued at no additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SARS Income Tax and VAT Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the automatic income tax number populated by the CIPC-SARS data interchange; activate SARS eFiling for the company; register as a VAT vendor only if taxable turnover in the next 12 months will exceed ZAR 1 million or if voluntary registration is commercially advisable; complete the EMP 101 and register for PAYE and UIF when the first employee is hired.
required_dossiers: Registered office address proof and bank confirmation
VAT 101 application with turnover estimates (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an income tax number is not generated within 20 business days, file the company income tax registration form at a SARS branch; for a delayed VAT application, escalate via eFiling case management and supply outstanding financial projections.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Employment and Labour (DEL); Compensation Fund; SARS; B-BBEE Commission
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as an employer for Unemployment Insurance Fund (UIF) and for Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act (COIDA) coverage; obtain the UIF reference number and a letter of good standing from the Compensation Fund; prepare an Exempt Micro Enterprise (EME) sworn B-BBEE affidavit before a commissioner of oaths when annual turnover is below ZAR 10 million; maintain records for tender and retail partner due diligence.
required_dossiers: Employee roster and ID copies (on first hire)
EME B-BBEE affidavit (commissioner of oaths witnessed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DEL records no registration after 30 days, resubmit the COIDA and UIF declarations at the provincial Labour Centre, obtain a stamped receipt, and escalate to the office manager; the B-BBEE affidavit may be sworn at any police station or commissioner of oaths.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - ISIC 4791 online retail of cosmetics triggers no industrial licensing board permit; product compliance is overseen by the Department of Health under the Foodstuffs, Cosmetics and Disinfectants Act 54 of 1972 (labeling, prohibitions and safety) and by the National Consumer Commission under the Consumer Protection Act 68 of 2008.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating or manufacturing permit required for online beauty retail; the entity must hold a valid municipal business premises and health clearance in the city of the registered office or warehouse and must comply with the Electronic Communications and Transactions Act 25 of 2002 for e-commerce disclosure requirements.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE) - environmental authorization authority under the National Environmental Management Act 107 of 1998 (NEMA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - office, warehouse and last-mile logistics activities of online retail are not listed under the 2014 EIA Regulations (Listing Notices 1-3, GN R. 982-984 as amended); no environmental authorization is required unless storage volumes exceed hazardous substance thresholds, which is unlikely for cosmetics retail
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial effluent or point-source air emissions are generated; general municipal sewer discharge limits and solid waste management obligations under the National Environmental Management: Waste Act 59 of 2008 apply; expired or damaged cosmetics must be disposed of as general waste through registered municipal streams.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993 compliance for the warehouse and office; fire-safety certificate and building occupancy clearance from the municipal fire department under SANS 10400 Part T prior to occupation; electrical Certificate of Compliance (CoC) for all leased premises; structural load verification for racking and storage areas; COIDA registration with the Compensation Fund for all employees; workplace first-aid, incident-reporting and equipment checks under the General Administrative Regulations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS), headed by the Commissioner for SARS; official portal: https://www.sars.gov.za; eFiling portal: https://www.sarsefiling.co.za
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A South African private company (Pty) Ltd is registered for income tax automatically upon incorporation through the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) integration with SARS; the company receives an income tax reference number. Where automatic activation is absent, the company must apply through SARS eFiling or a SARS branch using the prescribed registration applications and submit the certified memorandum of incorporation, Companies Registration Certificate, proof of physical and postal address, banking details, and identity documents of directors and shareholders. A foreign-owned or foreign-incorporated entity deriving taxable supplies from South Africa must apply for VAT registration using VAT 101 within 21 days after exceeding the compulsory VAT threshold; a single SARS taxpayer reference number covers income tax, VAT, PAYE, customs and other administered taxes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or analogous flow-through entity classification election exists under South African law; a (Pty) Ltd is mandatorily taxed at entity level as a resident company if incorporated in South Africa. Statutory tax elections are limited to specific corporate, group and hybrid mismatch provisions; South Africa applies hybrid mismatch rules under the Income Tax Act, including provisions addressing hybrid debt and hybrid equity instruments, and no entity-level classification election is available to recharacterise a (Pty) Ltd as a pass-through vehicle.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991, as amended, administered by SARS
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory VAT registration: ZAR 1,000,000 in taxable supplies within any 12-month period; voluntary VAT registration: ZAR 50,000 in taxable supplies within any 12-month period, subject to conditions including a minimum two-year registration period
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Africa has no general real-time electronic invoicing, fiscal clearance, API stamping or digital tax stamp mandate for standard VAT vendors as of the current compliance cycle. E-invoicing is permissible if the invoice satisfies the requirements of section 20 of the VAT Act; SARS may require certain categories of taxpayers to submit data electronically through eFiling or EDI-based channels, and in audit or verification engagements SARS may prescribe specific electronic export documentation formats, but no mandatory continuous fiscal clearance infrastructure is in force.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A vendor may apply the 0% VAT rate to exported movable goods where the goods are supplied to a non-resident recipient and the goods are removed from South Africa within 90 days after the date of supply, or where the vendor itself exports the goods, and the prescribed documentary proof under section 55 of the VAT Act is retained. For services, zero-rating is available when the services are supplied to a non-resident recipient and are not performed in South Africa or are not supplied directly in connection with movable property situated in South Africa; the vendor must obtain and retain sufficient commercial evidence to show the recipient is outside South Africa and that the services are exported.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing removal from South Africa
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank confirmation of receipt of export payment in foreign currency
Commercial invoice and packing list identifying the exported cosmetic goods
Certified copy of the non-resident recipient's identity, registration or address evidence
Proof of delivery or logistics tracking documentation supporting the export route
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS rigorously audits export zero-rating claims; if the vendor cannot produce the prescribed customs, logistics and foreign-currency remittance documents, SARS will raise an additional VAT assessment at 15% on the full supply value, with statutory interest. Under the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011, an understatement penalty may be imposed of up to 200% of the tax shortfall depending on conduct, and the Value-Added Tax Act permits additional penalties and criminal prosecution for fraudulent or knowingly false export declarations or tax invoices. Clawback exposure is retrospective and SARS may disallow input tax credits associated with an export transaction where the export conditions are not evidenced to SARS's satisfaction.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), acting through the Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv) under the Currency and Exchanges Act, 9 of 1933 and the Exchange Control Regulations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South African rand (ZAR) is convertible for current account transactions, including trade-in-goods and services, cross-border fees, and dividends, subject to documentation and authorisation-dealer oversight. Capital account transactions are restricted under South Africa's exchange control regime; inward equity contributions, shareholder loans, and outward loan repayments or portfolio investments require FinSurv approval, a designated Authorised Dealer, and the filing of prescribed capital-flow returns. Profit remittances of after-tax distributable profits are permitted, but must be supported by audited financial statements, a tax clearance certificate, and a completed outward payment form. Synthetic convertibility constraints are present for an online DTC retail business because payment gateway settlements from Shopfify/PayPal are usually aggregated and may be routed through foreign payment processors, requiring reconciliation with underlying sales invoices to avoid adverse classification as 'mixed remittances' or 'unidentified inward transfers'.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be received in South Africa through an authorised dealer within 180 days of the date of shipment. The exporter must provide a customs export declaration and the relevant invoice. There is no mandatory conversion ratio into ZAR; export receipts may be credited to a Foreign Currency Account (FCA) held with an authorised dealer. The export proceeds must be repatriated in full and may be retained in the FCA indefinitely, provided the exporter completes periodic compliance reporting to SARB FinSurv and the authorised dealer. For online cosmetics retail, all Shopify and PayPal settlement flows that are generated by sale of goods to non-residents constitute export proceeds and must be recorded and settled into the company's local FCA or ZAR account within the statutory 180-day window rather than being held permanently offshore.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: FEASIBILITY_RATING: Medium-to-Low for use as a primary treasury rail. Offshore digital EMI service providers such as Wise, Payoneer, and Airwallex are not licensed as banks in South Africa and cannot provide a South African domestic clearing account or access to the national payment system. They may operate legally as cross-border settlement agents for inbound and outbound flows, subject to the company's ultimate reliance on a licensed authorised dealer. The Banks Act, 94 of 1990 and the National Payment System Act, 78 of 1998 prohibit unlicensed entities from accepting deposits or providing payment aggregation services to South African residents without a banking or PSP license. Therefore, the feasible use is limited to: (i) collection of retail card sales in foreign currencies via Shopfify/PayPal, (ii) settlement into a ZAR bank account through a registered payment intermediary, and (iii) managing a notional multi-currency ledger; it cannot replace the domestic corporate bank account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: FICA does not contain a strict statutory requirement that directors appear physically at a bank branch. Major South African banks, however, apply a risk-based onboarding policy and, for a company with non-resident shareholders and no local physical footprint, will normally require a video-verified KYC interview with the Ultimate Beneficial Owner and at least one authorised signatory. A notarised copy of each director's passport, a board resolution, apostilled incorporation documents, and a certificate of residential address are accepted. Some banks permit remote on-boarding where the existing relationship is low-risk; nevertheless, to mitigate shell-company indicators, the bank is likely to insist on physical verification of the single local director or a mandated attorney-in-fact at a South African branch. In all cases, a liveness check and source-of-funds questionnaire will be completed remotely or in person.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident corporate shareholder structure with no South African physical office
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Memorandum of Incorporation, share register and UBO declarations, notarised board resolution appointing a local authorised signatory, signed-off lease agreement or serviced-office agreement in Gauteng, and six months of projected bank statements demonstrating operational substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-value digital retail receipts from Shopfify/PayPal settling from multiple foreign processors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Platform settlement reports, a reconciliation ledger mapping each settlement to the underlying sales invoices, customer IP-level geotagging data, and a clear breakdown showing no crypto-related currency flows or transaction-laundering patterns.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inward shareholder loan / capital injection classified as a 'covered foreign entity' or 'suspicious financing'
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed shareholders' resolution, subscription agreement or loan agreement, annotated SWIFT MT103 with the correct BOP purpose code, proof of the corporate ownership chain, and the company's external tax advisor's confirmation that the transaction is not a back-to-back loan or disguised dividend.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Retail end-customers located in high-risk sanctions-controlled countries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shopify store terms of sale excluding delivery to sanctioned countries, real-time IP/geoblock settings, KYC/AML screening log of all customer transactions, and an audit trail demonstrating that payment cards issued in high-risk jurisdictions are automatically declined.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions must be routed via SWIFT MT103 from the foreign shareholder's bank directly to the South African authorised dealer with the company's bank account as ultimate credit. The wire must carry the explicit purpose code corresponding to 'direct equity investment' or 'intercompany shareholder loan' on the inward BOP declaration and the recipient's unique corporate reference. For an amount above ZAR 10 million equivalent, a prior exchange control approval from FinSurv is required; the authorised dealer will issue a Certificate of Capital Import. The company should maintain a capital escrow ledger, evidence of the underlying board resolution, and a statement of funding purpose to prevent reclassification of the injection as outstanding trade debt or a taxable local loan.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound supplier payments for cosmetics inventory, packaging, marketing, and logistics are carried through the South African banking system using SWIFT MT103 (regular direct remittance), SWIFT MT202 for correspondent bank cover, or a commercial letter of credit (MT700/MT720) for larger wholesale consignments. All outward payments must be supported by invoices and proof of trade and reported under the authorised dealer's outward payment form, citing the appropriate trade/service purpose code. Same-day ZAR-to-ZAR clearing can utilise SAMOS for local suppliers, but any USD/EUR payment to a foreign beneficiary must be settled via the authorised dealer's FX desk. The documentary requirement includes the supplier quotation, commercial invoice, bill of lading/airway bill, and procurement contract to justify the payment and match the approved exposure horizon.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla outright deliverable FX forward for USD, EUR, and GBP trade exposures with a maximum 12-month tenor and documentary underlying exposure.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) — permissible only for synthetic offset of ZAR exposure through an authorised dealer, subject to FinSurv approval and the requirement that the exposure is genuine and not speculative.
Cross-currency swap (CCS) between ZAR and USD/EUR for matched capital inflows or long-term procurement contracts, requiring FinSurv authorisation for tenors exceeding 24 months.
European-style FX options purchased to hedge procurement upside and cap adverse moves in the cosmetic ingredients supply chain; option premia may be paid in ZAR.
FX swap or same-day swap/forward to roll over a maturing post-shipment receivable or payable without increasing the company's net open foreign-currency position.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CIPC Annual Return (Notice of Annual Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after each anniversary of the company's incorporation date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A late filing penalty of ZAR 100 per month or part thereof applies; failure to file for two consecutive years triggers CIPC involuntary strike-off proceedings and can result in director disqualification.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CIPC Beneficial Ownership Return (Annual Confirmation and Change Filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Confirmation is submitted as part of the CIPC Annual Return; any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be filed within 10 business days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing within the prescribed period constitutes an offence under the Companies Act 71 of 2008, with potential fines of up to ZAR 500,000, administrative penalties, and criminal liability for directors.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (AFS) for Shareholders and Regulatory Review
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders and, where prescribed, CIPC or the Company's Auditor
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements must be prepared and presented to shareholders within 6 months after the company's financial year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CIPC may issue a compliance notice; if a compulsory audit is omitted, directors face administrative fines up to ZAR 1,000,000 and possible imprisonment for repeated non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (ITR14) for Profit Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual corporate income tax return must be filed within 12 months after the company's financial year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly late-filing penalty of up to 10% of assessed tax under Section 210 of the Tax Administration Act, plus interest at the prescribed rate; repeated non-compliance may lead to criminal prosecution and obstruction of trading.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory audit is mandatory if the Public Interest Score (PI Score) is 500 or higher, or if the company is a public company, state-owned company, or otherwise regulated by a directive. If the PI Score is between 100 and 499, an independent review is required. A PI Score below 100 with compiled annual financial statements is sufficient for a private company.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as issued by the IASB, or IFRS for SMEs for eligible non-public companies; South African professional standards recognize both frameworks.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The CIPC Annual Return must be accompanied by a confirmation of beneficial ownership information. Any transfer of shares or change in beneficial ownership must be recorded in the company's Beneficial Ownership Register immediately and the Beneficial Ownership Return must be submitted to CIPC within 10 business days of the change.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% for years of assessment commencing on or after 1 April 2022 (reduced from 28%); companies, close corporations and trusts are taxed at 27% above the Small Business Corporation bands
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No specific holiday for ISIC 4791. General relief: (i) Small Business Corporation (SBC) concessionary rates if gross income ≤ R20 million and not more than 10% from investment/rendering of personal services - 0% on first R95,500; 7% on band R95,501–R365,000; 21% on band R365,001–R550,000; 27% above; (ii) s.12E accelerated capital allowances for SBCs on manufacturing assets (minimal retail relevance); (iii) s.11(a) general deductions and s.11(i) wear-and-tear allowances on website/point-of-sale IT equipment; (iv) Youth Employment Tax Incentive of up to R1,500 per qualifying employee (Hiree <29 years, c.23(if)), employer top-up incentives? Actually it's an employment tax incentive via PAYE reduction; (v) no VAT-specific CIT relief.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite carry-forward with no expiry (s.20 Income Tax Act); however, from years of assessment commencing on or after 1 April 2022, an assessed loss may be set off only against 80% of current-year taxable income, leaving a 20% taxable base before loss utilization.
